---
title: "Curating the data, part 1: Finn the Wolfhound"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(here)
library(tidyr)
library(tidytext)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load the perfectly cleaned data from Step 1
load(here("data/finn_with_chapters.rda"))
```
```{r}
data(stop_words)

# 2. Tokenize the text directly from the Step 1 data
finn_clean <- finn_with_chapters |> 
  # Chop into words
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text, token = "words") |>
  # Remove stop words
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  # Rename your chapter column so it matches the rest of your scripts!
  rename(chapter = chapter_number)

# Save the final, clean, tokenized data to use in your sentiment analysis!
save(finn_clean, file = here("data/finn_clean.rda"))

# Check the unique words and total row count
unique(finn_clean$word) |> length()
nrow(finn_clean)
```
